recap.text: Borant claims Earth as a mining claim under Syndicate law and uses the dungeon as legal cover and revenue. The company earns money from advertising, a government stipend, and patron commissions. Mordecai warns that crawlers who disparage the corporation on camera may have their experience accelerated. Odette advises Carl never to say mud skipper.

An announcement states there are nearly 40,000 classes among just under 700,000 crawlers. Borant sets the experience counter for citizens to zero and boosts city guard stats to protect non-combatant NPCs. Borant burns its one seasonal veto to void eighty-three Celestial boxes, though it remains liable for one box opened before the appeal.

Borant announces that the bubble-escape method stays legal after litigation and input from the Syndicate. Some secondary summonings are blocked because escaping ferals had a 66 percent chance of calling a matching deity, which could cause an extinction-level event. Sponsorship bidding for the sixth floor is 33 percent of projections. Third-party tourists paid by an anonymous sponsor will hunt crawlers on the sixth floor.

Borant claims the Valtay news means nothing and she is not leaving her personal life project. Sponsors may sell stakes, hunters cannot communicate outside the dungeon, and the southwestern hot springs cooked the crawlers in them. Borant attempts to stop Prepotente with peace bonding, freeze, paralysis, slow, a teleport, and an Administrative Hold. The AI negates the attack and vanishes four gnolls with guns in smoke.

beats.headline: The foreclosure
beats.text: It claims Earth under Syndicate law and turns the planet into a mining claim. The dungeon is the legal cover and the revenue at once.
beats.gist: The Borant Corporation claims Earth as a mining claim and uses the dungeon as legal cover.

beats.headline: Say the name and it is recorded
beats.text: The mining is almost incidental; what Borant takes fits on a single transport. The money is the show: advertising, a stipend from the Syndicate government, and a commission on every credit a patron spends. When Carl asks, Mordecai's voice turns formal. Any crawler who names the government or the sponsoring corporation is recorded for review, and one found disparaging them, especially on camera, may have the experience "accelerated". NPCs are required to say the name repeatedly during training, so they are mostly ignored. The company, he adds, takes its image quite seriously.
beats.gist: Borant makes money through advertising, government stipends, and patron commissions.

beats.headline: Never say mud skipper
beats.text: Odette's advice, in a room Borant cannot hear: never say mud skipper in the dungeon. The kua-tin tried to have the word listed as hate speech with the Syndicate, and hardly anyone used it until they did. Nobody likes the kua-tin government. Borant is a different story; some of them only want to put on a good show, and they were incensed to be forced into this early release. And all indentureship contracts freeze during a bankruptcy seizure action, which, she says, is nothing the crawlers need to worry about.
beats.gist: Odette advises against saying mud skipper because the kua-tin government is disliked.

beats.headline: Citizens worth zero experience
beats.text: The announcement after the recap: nearly 40,000 different classes among just under 700,000 crawlers, a record. Potential sponsors may now put in early bids. And a general warning against violence toward non-combatant NPCs. It is not technically against the rules, but Borant wishes to keep the citizenry as safe as possible, so the experience counter for citizens is now zero and city guards get a slight boost in stats. Carl asks what that is about. Mordecai does not know.
beats.gist: Borant announces a record 40,000 classes among under 700,000 crawlers and opens early bids for sponsors.

beats.headline: It burns a veto rather than pay
beats.text: Eighty-three Celestial boxes are owed. Borant appeals, a Syndicate court overrules it, and it burns its one seasonal veto to void the prizes anyway, which has never been done this early. It is still liable for the one box that was opened before the appeal. A production company that cheap has seams worth looking for.
beats.gist: Borant burns its seasonal veto to void eighty-three Celestial boxes owed after a court overrules its appeal.

beats.headline: The bubble escape stays legal
beats.text: The day's announcement. After careful discussion, litigation Borant won, and input from the Syndicate, the bubble-escape method may continue. Some secondary summonings are now blocked: each escaping feral had a 66 percent chance of calling a matching deity, and one of the gods summoned would have been an extinction-level event for this floor and the next. Sponsorship bidding for the sixth floor stands at 33 percent of projections, and nobody wants it lower. Then some sixth-floor notes: specialisation on descent, and third-party tourists who will be hunting crawlers, their entry fees paid by an anonymous sponsor.
beats.gist: Borant announces that the bubble-escape method stays legal after litigation and Syndicate input.

beats.headline: Nothing has changed, says Borant
beats.text: The announcer is chipper. The Valtay news means nothing, she says: Borant is still a kua-tin organisation, severed from the civil war that has just erupted at home, and this crawl is her personal life project and she is going nowhere. Then the notes. Sponsors may sell their stakes starting next floor. Over 500 crawlers are claimed and over 50 hunters have fallen. Hunters may no longer communicate with anyone outside the dungeon. The southwestern hot springs were turned up, cooking the crawlers in them. Crawlers in the top 1,000 can now see their rankings.
beats.gist: Borant says the Valtay news means nothing and her personal life project continues.

beats.headline: Blocked by its own rules
beats.text: Borant wants Prepotente stopped before he can touch the seventh floor. In the pole position chamber a whole line of debuffs hits him and the crawlers with him: peace bonding, freeze, paralysis, slow, a teleport, an Administrative Hold. Four gnolls with guns appear. Every one of them is negated by AI resolution, and the gnolls vanish in smoke. The AI, Prepotente says, is forcing Borant to follow its own rules.
beats.gist: Borant uses debuffs and gnolls to stop Prepotente, but the AI forces Borant to follow its rules.
